General commercial policy does not reimburse provider preventable conditions. For inpatient DRG-based claims, HAC-related charges and days are removed from the DRG calculation when POA indicates the condition was not present on admission. Never events tied to wrong patient, wrong body part, wrong surgery, or retained foreign object are denied.

output.elevance_executive_summary: Elevance has dedicated reimbursement policies for Maternity Services, including a current policy effective 01/01/2026 and a prior version, which directly applies to cesarean delivery claims. Elevance also maintains Provider Preventable Conditions policies that can affect inpatient maternity reimbursement when preventable conditions are present.

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: Apply the Y65.53, Y65.52, and Y65.51 DRG edit only to related services in the same procedure episode on the same inpatient claim, with the POA indicator present on claim; exclude cases where the condition existed prior to treatment by that facility, where a secondary facility treated the HAC caused by another facility, or where provider, state, or federal contracts and/or mandates indicate otherwise. Apply to CA. Exempt: condition existed prior to treatment by that facility, secondary facility treated the HAC caused by another facility, provider, state, or federal contracts and/or mandates indicate otherwise. Peer: Elevance Health (external) and Elevance Health (internal) both anchor these controls at the DRG level, supporting a single inpatient DRG edit for cesarean admissions..

IA — For CA cesarean delivery inpatient DRG claims, require Y65.53, Y65.52, or Y65.51 to be reported on the same inpatient claim with modifier PA, PB, or PC and a POA indicator present on claim before it is used in the DRG reimbursement calculation. (CA) Elevance Health (external) and Elevance Health (internal) both place this Provider Preventable Conditions logic in DRG scope, so the cesarean control should run on the inpatient DRG claim..
